title: High-resolution Patterned Biofilm Deposition Using pDawn-Ag43
protocol: Transform pDawn-Ag43 into an E. coli strain of interest.
Inoculate the E. coli strain hosting pDawn-Ag43 plasmid into LB broth supplemented with 50 μg/mL spectinomycin (LB+spec) and grow overnight in a shaking incubator at ~250 rpm, 37 °C.
Harvest the purified pDawn-Ag43 plasmid using a miniprep kit.
Generate competent stocks of the chosen E. coli strain following an established protocol.
Transform the pDawn-Ag43 plasmid into the competent bacteria.
Allow transformed bacteria to recover for 1 hour, then plate on LB+spec agar plates.
Incubate the plated samples overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate a single colony of pDawn-Ag43 from an LB+spec agar plate into LB+spec broth and grow it in a shaking incubator (at ~250 rpm, 37 °C) to exponential phase (OD600 ~0.4 - 0.8).
Prepare a long-term storage stock by mixing 1 mL of culture with 1 mL of 50% sterile glycerol.
Store the mixture in a cryo-tube containing a 25% glycerol freezer stock at -80 °C.
Create competent cells from the pDawn-Ag43 transformed strain.
Repeat the transformation process for additional plasmids as needed using the competent cells.
Obtain a bacterial incubator with non-transparent walls and a hole for passing cables.
Acquire a portable projector capable of fitting and functioning inside the bacterial incubator.
Equip a laptop with software for presentation-projection.
Ensure that the minimal focus distance of the projector is less than the interior height of the incubator.
Place the projector inside the incubator at the bottom, with the aperture pointing directly upward.
Construct a set-up with an optical breadboard base connected to a vertical post.
Connect the horizontal post to the vertical post and screw it into the projector.
Securely fix the projector near the bottom of the incubator, ensuring the aperture points upward.
Cover reflective surfaces inside the incubator with dark matte materials to minimize reflections.
Attach an empty 'dummy' culture dish to the ceiling of the incubator using tape.
Adjust the focus on the projector by turning the focusing knob until the image is sharp and clear on the bottom surface of the 'dummy' culture dish.
Remove the 'dummy' culture dish once the projection has been optimized.
Direct the projector to illuminate the full field of view with maximum blue illumination (e.g., RGB = [0, 0, 255]) by presenting a full blue slide.
Place the photodetector head at the incubator ceiling.
Read the intensity on the corresponding power meter calibrated to light wavelength 460 nm.
Reduce ambient light as much as possible prior to making illumination intensity measurements.
Adjust the illumination intensity using an adjustable neutral density filter placed at the projector aperture.
Rotate the filter to adjust the illumination intensity measured by the power meter until it reads 50 μW/cm² in the center of the blue-light projected region.
Draw arbitrary patterns using the presentation/projector software on the laptop.
Display these patterns on the ceiling of the incubator.
Streak a pDawn-Ag43 strain from glycerol stock onto LB+spec agar plates.
Allow colonies to grow overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate a colony of pDawn-Ag43 bacteria from an agar plate in LB+spec broth.
Grow the culture overnight to stationary phase in a shaking incubator at ~250 rpm, 37 °C for ~16 h.
Subdilute the culture at a ratio of 1:1,000 with LB+spec broth by adding 1 μL of overnight culture to 1 mL of fresh LB+spec.
Allow the subdiluted culture to grow until late exponential/early stationary phase (OD ~1.0) for ~6 h in a shaking incubator at ~250 rpm, 37 °C.
Prepare M63 media with 1x M63 salts, 1 mM MgSO4, 0.2% glucose, 0.1% casamino acids, and 50 μg/mL spectinomycin in water.
Subdilute the late-exponential-phase culture at a ratio of 1:100 with M63 media supplemented with 0.1% casamino acids and 50 μg/mL spectinomycin.
Introduce the dilution into a biofilm culture dish by pipetting.
Tape the culture dish to the ceiling of the incubator for illumination from below by the projector.
Ensure that the surface at the bottom of the dish is transparent for illumination.
Allow the biofilms to culture in the incubator overnight at 37 °C without shaking.
Remove the culture dish from the incubator after culturing.
Discard the liquid media by gently aspirating with a pipette.
Rinse the sample twice with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution.
Gently pipette in PBS and then aspirate to remove remaining planktonic cells.
If fluorescently tagged, image the samples using fluorescence microscopy.
Apply one drop of mounting medium to a biofilm sample for preservation if needed.
Cover the sample with a glass coverslip without capturing any bubbles underneath.
Allow the mounting medium to harden overnight before imaging.
If not fluorescently tagged, apply crystal violet stain technique to enhance contrast prior to imaging.
Grow pDawn-Ag43 bacteria on different surfaces.
Put glass or poly-dimethyl-siloxane (PDMS) coupons into well plates prior to adding a bacterial sample/illumination.
Follow the same protocol to pattern pDawn-ag43 biofilms on glass and PDMS.
Generate a culture chamber mold for PDMS.
Attach a hard, rectangular prism to a flat surface to create a cavity in the PDMS that serves as the culture chamber.
Pour PDMS into the mold and allow it to cure.
Trim any excess PDMS after curing.
Punch inlet/outlet channels into the cavity/culture chamber.
Bond the cavity to a flat surface by firmly pressing the PDMS onto the surface, leaving the cavity between the surface and the PDMS ceiling as the biofilm culture chamber.
Use a syringe with blunt tip needles to introduce the bacterial sample into the culture chamber.
Rinse the culture chamber with PBS buffer.
Grow pDawn-Ag43 bacteria using a film photomask for structured illumination.
Design a biofilm pattern using CAD software compatible with a film photomask printer/print service.
Send the photomask file to the printer/printing service and await the return of the physical photomask.
Instruct the projector to illuminate a full field of view with maximum blue illumination (e.g., RGB = [0, 0, 255]).
Cut out a region of interest from the larger film photomask.
Tape the cut-out region directly to the bottom of the biofilm culture dish prior to introducing the bacterial sample for overnight illumination.
Culture the biofilms as before and remove the photomask after culturing, prior to imaging.
